title: Exploring the association between big five personality traits and healthy eating habits among university students in Jordan.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Personality traits are the fundamental components that influence characteristics, attitude, and thought processes, distinguishing individuals from each other. According to the most accepted model, Open-Mindedness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Negative Emotionality are considered the five major traits that everyone possesses; however, their levels vary among individuals. These are shaped by genetic and environmental factors, with various influences as contributors.
OBJECTIVES: To explore the connection between personality traits and healthy eating habits.
METHODOLOGY: A survey with four sections was conducted and posted on social media platforms. These include: Demographics, Personality analysis, Academic status, and Healthy food score. This study utilized the Big Five Inventory-2 (BFI-2) to assess personality traits and the Adolescent Food Habits Checklist (AFHC) to measure dietary habits.
RESULTS: A total of 389 university students from Jordan (average age 21.9 years, SD of 2.9) participated in the study. The average healthy food score was 10.2, indicating poor healthy eating habits (maximum score 23 signifies better healthy eating habits). Regarding the Big Five traits, participants scored highest on Agreeableness (mean of 75.5%) and lowest on Negative Emotionality (mean of 58.8%). Results showed that Conscientiousness is positively correlated with AFHC score; however, higher Negative Emotionality scores were associated with a poor healthy diet, which corresponds to a lower AFHC score. Other Big Five traits were not significantly correlated with AFHC scores.
CONCLUSION: Some personality traits were associated with eating habits among university students in Jordan. Further research is needed to examine other factors affecting the eating habits of university students in Jordan.
